subject: Post-demo: Operational criteria & reservation pathways for NexaSecure POC
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Benjamin Cho <benjamin.cho@nexasecure.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed test matrix and asks

Ben — thanks for the time today, really appreciate the thoughtful questions from engineering and procurement. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can line up a side-by-side POC that directly compares Redwood Dedicated vs the hyperscaler reserved path you mentioned.

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Target p95 latency: 200–300ms for the main inference endpoint (batch size 1, single-turn).
- Expected steady concurrency: ~200 active requests during peak windows; spikes up to ~350 for short bursts.
- Procurement interest: 12‑month commit or committed spend; wants clear SLA/credits and audit artifacts (SOC2, data flow diagrams).

What we propose (short checklist / next steps):
1) Share the attached test matrix (redwood-postdemo-matrix.xlsx) — outlines 4 core tests: tail latency, sustained throughput, failover & cold-start behavior, and cost-per-1M tokens estimate.
2) Confirm data handling constraints for the POC (PII? retention window?). Please send the short requirements PDF you mentioned — procurement said they would surface it.
3) Redwood will stand up a Dedicated pool (config: ~16 A100-equivalent GPUs) for a 72‑hour soak + 24h burst window. Hyperscaler side — we need the reserved SKU they want us to test so we can reproduce node sizes and network topology.
4) Schedule a 30–60 minute kickoff with your infra and procurement next week to lock down times and acceptance criteria.

Attachments: redwood-postdemo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Links: HubSpot deal + shared drive with test plan (I will send once we confirm kickoff).

If the plan looks good I’ll follow up with a proposed POC calendar and a ballpark cost delta for reserved vs dedicated to set expectations for procurement.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

---

From: Benjamin Cho <benjamin.cho@nexasecure.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: NexaSecure Procurement <procurement@nexasecure.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 13:45:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed test matrix and asks

Thanks, Evelyn — good summary. A few clarifications from our side after we debriefed: 

- Data: PII will be redacted before it hits the inference layer for the POC; however, we need confirmation on retention: anything stored in logs must be purged within 7 days.
- SLA: Procurement would prefer a 99.9% availability target for production; for the POC they want measurable uptime and a runbook for failover.
- Reserved SKU: we are considering the hyperscaler "c5g-large-gpu-reserved" family (we'll confirm exact SKU by EOD). Procurement is also asking for an ARR vs committed‑compute comparison (they want to understand unit economics).
- SOC2: I attached a short requirements checklist and procurement asked for a copy of your SOC2 attestation and controls overview — if you can point us to a hosted copy, that would speed things up.

We can do a kickoff next Tue or Wed morning PST. Also happy for your infra lead to speak directly with our platform team to align on network egress and IP allowlists.

Best —
Benjamin Cho
Head of Platform Engineering, NexaSecure
benjamin.cho@nexasecure.com | +1 617-555-2210

Attachments: nexasecure-poc-requirements.pdf (pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:03:10 -0700
Subject: Internal: NexaSecure POC — blueprint and owners

Quick internal note to align on deliverables before we respond to procurement: 

1) POC configuration: set up a Dedicated pool sized to replicate their production target (provision ~16 A100-equivalent GPUs). This will let us demonstrate tail-latency benefits from our KV cache + continuous batching.
2) Hyperscaler parity: replicate expected reserved VM SKU once they confirm exact instance. We'll document differences (networking, pre-warm strategy, ephemeral vs pinned NVMe).
3) Acceptance criteria (we should propose):
   - p95 <= 300ms on single-turn generation at steady state (concurrency 200)
   - <5% request error rate during 72-hour soak
   - documented failover: simulate losing 2 nodes and show traffic routing + warmup metrics
4) Tests & timing: Jordan—can you schedule two 6-hour benchmark windows next week (one for steady-state, one for cold-start + failover)? Karthik—can you draft pricing delta slides (reserved hyperscaler vs dedicated commit) with a per-1M-token estimate?
5) Security artifacts: point them to our hosted SOC2 report link and the private Drive folder with logs retention policy. Evelyn—I'll prepare a short runbook for failover behaviour to include in the shared Drive.

Let's keep the external reply crisp and put a proposed kickoff window (Tue/Wed morning PST) and the Drive + DocuSign links.

Rishi
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Benjamin Cho <benjamin.cho@nexasecure.com>, NexaSecure Procurement <procurement@nexasecure.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed test matrix and asks

Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround and the checklist. Confirming next steps and a short mutual action plan so procurement has a single doc to work from.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- This week: Redwood shares SOC2 link + Drive folder with proposed test matrix and runbook (we've attached the matrix; Drive link below).
- Next Tue/Wed (you pick a morning PST): kickoff call + infra alignment (Jordan will coordinate).
- Week after kickoff: 72-hour Dedicated soak (Redwood-provisioned) and equivalent reserved-hyperscaler test (we will mirror the reserved SKU you confirm).
- Acceptance: p95 <= 300ms, error rate <5% during soak; documented behaviour and failover runbook sign-off by NexaSecure platform team.
- Commercial: Redwood will provide a ballpark committed pricing comparison ahead of the POC; procurement to provide preferred reserved SKU and any PO/contract constraints prior to kickoff.

Links and attachments:
- Shared Drive (POC test plan & runbook): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-nexasecure-poc
- SOC2 report (public copy): https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-report.pdf
- DocuSign (MSA template for a committed path): https://na.docusign.net/EXAMPLE-NX-MSA
- Attached: redwood-postdemo-matrix.xlsx

Ben — can you confirm: (1) preferred kickoff day (Tue/Wed morning PST), and (2) the exact hyperscaler reserved SKU so we can reproduce it for parity testing? Once you confirm those two items we’ll publish the calendar invite and the detailed test timetable.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a short, tight POC.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
